title_gaddi: गद्दी चरे भेड़ें, ते भेड़ें चरन गद्दी
source_citation: Shashi (1977), p. 62; Kumari et al. (2026), p. 19
summary_en: Literal: 'The Gaddi grazes the sheep, and the sheep graze the Gaddi.' Expresses the profound, inseparable symbiotic bond between the shepherd and his flock: the shepherd's entire life, sustenance, clothing, and mobility depend upon the animals he cares for.
text_excerpt_gaddi: गद्दी चरे भेड़ें, ते भेड़ें चरन गद्दी।
text_excerpt_en: The Gaddi feeds the sheep, and the sheep sustain the Gaddi.

summary_en: Literal: 'When the forest empties in winter, the Gaddi settles down.' Describes the seasonal transhumance cycle: when cold weather and snow force people out of the high pastures, the Gaddi shepherd moves down to winter villages in the foothills.
text_excerpt_en: When the wilderness empties, the Gaddi makes his camp.

title_gaddi: भरमौर दा बसना, शिवा दा असना
summary_en: Literal: 'To dwell in Bharmaur is to reside in the abode of Shiva.' Expresses the deep religious belief that Bharmaur is consecrated sacred ground directly under the gaze of Mount Manimahesh Kailash.
text_excerpt_gaddi: भरमौर दा बसना, शिवा दा असना।
text_excerpt_en: To live in Bharmaur is to reside in the presence of Shiva.

title_gaddi: पुहाला दा ध्यान धार पुर, ते भेड़ां दा मुंह घास पुर
source_citation: Nirmohi, Saraz: Lok Aur Parampara, p. 102
summary_en: Literal: 'The shepherd's eyes are on the mountain ridge, while the sheep's mouth is in the grass.' A shepherd must remain ever watchful of weather changes and predators while the flock grazes peacefully.
text_excerpt_gaddi: पुहाला दा ध्यान धार पुर, ते भेड़ां दा मुंह घास पुर।
text_excerpt_en: The shepherd watches the ridge, while the sheep graze the grass.

title_gaddi: मणिमहेश दा पाणी, रोगां दी हाणी
summary_en: Literal: 'The water of Lake Manimahesh destroys all disease.' Traditional pilgrim belief praising the sacred and curative virtues of the high glacial lake at the base of Mount Kailash.
text_excerpt_gaddi: मणिमहेश दा पाणी, रोगां दी हाणी।
text_excerpt_en: The water of Manimahesh is the destroyer of afflictions.

title_gaddi: चोला पूरा ऊन दा, सर्दी नू भुल दा
summary_en: Literal: 'A coat of pure wool forgets all cold.' Celebrates the heavy hand-spun sheep wool chola that allows Gaddi shepherds to survive sub-zero mountain nights.
text_excerpt_gaddi: चोला पूरा ऊन दा, सर्दी नू भुल दा।
text_excerpt_en: A coat made of pure wool forgets the cold.
